San Francisco Planning, Article 10 landmark designation: Landmark No. 336, House of Latin Rock (landmark designation report and ordinance)
sources.label: SF Planning, landmark designation

historical_record.description: Built as a semi-attached, one-story-over-basement single-family house: wood frame clad in stucco, with a front gable and pent and shed roofs in red clay tile, two arched ground-floor openings and a boxed oriel bay facing York Street.
The South Mission Historic Resource Survey found the property ineligible for the California Register; the mural had not yet been painted.

The "Casa Bandido" mural, also called "Take It From the Top: Latin Rock," was painted in acrylic over every exterior surface of the house by lead artists Max Marttila and Fred Alvarado with youth artists of the Precita Eyes Urban Youth Arts Program, assisted by Margaret White and Marina Perez-Wong, funded by a grant distributed through Precita Eyes.

The finished mural depicts more than eighty-seven Latin rock musicians and bands of the Mission District, among them Carlos Santana, Malo (formerly the Malibus) and salsa singer Maria Medina, set among Aztec and Chicano motifs, a jukebox version of Mission Dolores and an altar to musicians who have died.
The Board of Supervisors adopted Resolution No. 120-26 initiating landmark designation of the house; the Mayor signed it on March 6, 2026.
The Historic Preservation Commission recommended landmark designation (Resolution No. 1565).
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 336, House of Latin Rock and the "Casa Bandido" mural.

unknowns: The mural is dated both 2017 and 2015.

notable_residents.name: Michael Rios
notable_residents.detail: Chicano artist and muralist Michael Rios lived and worked in the house during the 1990s, the decade he painted stage backdrops for Santana, one of which became the cover of the 1999 album Supernatural.
